text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 8.1% today, bringing its two-week loss to 16%, likely driven by disappointing quarterly earnings or guidance announced yesterday combined with a broader market reassessment of refiner profitability. Refinery utilization sits at 94.5%—already near capacity—while gasoline and diesel inventories remain elevated (208.9 million and 99.3 million barrels respectively), suggesting limited room for refiners to boost production or margins even as crude prices hover around $100 per barrel.

The sell-off reflects a structural headwind: with refinery capacity constrained and fuel inventories high, the typical profit engine for refiners (the margin between crude input and product output) faces pressure going forward. The political shift toward renewable energy, combined with oil price uncertainty flagged by industry executives, has also likely prompted investors to reassess the investment thesis for traditional energy companies.
